title: The arm and the heart
hookLine: the arm box sits on the upper arm, facing the heart, so action and feeling join

cards: Lift your left arm and bend it, as if to make a muscle. Notice where the top of your arm rests: right up against the side of your chest, close to your heart. If you're left-handed, try it on the right.
That spot, the soft part of the upper arm just above the elbow, is exactly where the first box goes. And it isn't placed just anywhere.
It's angled, very slightly, so that when the arm is lowered, the box leans in toward the heart.

teach.h: SHEL YAD: THE ONE OF THE HAND.
teach.b: The arm box is called the shel yad, the one of the hand. The Torah says bind them upon thy hand, and the rabbis read hand here as the upper arm, the muscle that moves the hand.

They placed it on the weaker arm, the left for a right-handed person, because the verse's wording hinted at it, and so the strong hand could do the binding. The box sits on the bicep, facing the heart. Why the heart?

teach.h: IN YOUR HEART, UPON YOUR HAND.
teach.b: Because another verse, right beside the command about binding, says: "Therefore shall ye lay up these My words in your heart and in your soul; and ye shall bind them for a sign upon your hand."
Heart and hand, in one breath.

So the rabbis taught that the box on the arm should be across from the heart, and later teachers draw the lesson: the arm is what you do, the heart is what you feel and want, and this practice ties them together.
On this reading, a good feeling that never moves the hand falls short, and so does a deed done without the heart. The arm box goes on first, with a blessing.
Then the strap is wound around the forearm, usually seven times, down toward the hand.
There's also a tradition that the arm box is covered, by a sleeve or the prayer shawl, while the head box is visible: one a private sign, the other a public one.
And that's the week: Purim's gifts, the seder's questions, the Omer's count, Shavuot's gift, Tisha B'Av's floor, the boxes, and now the arm against the heart.

how: When putting on tefillin, the arm box is placed first on the upper weaker arm, angled toward the heart, with a blessing; its strap is then wound around the forearm, usually seven times.

practice: Place one hand flat on your chest and feel your heartbeat, or just the warmth.
Think of one thing you have to decide or do today, a message, a conversation, a purchase, and ask two questions: what do I want to do, and what do I actually feel?
Wait until they point the same way, or at least until you know where they differ.
